rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking the earth and eating its provision culminate in resurrection to God: return to the Creator and answer before Him.
rows.anchor: bütün o yürüyüşlerin, yiyişlerin gayesi O’na müntehî olan bir nüşûrdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the earth docile and granted people the power to walk on it; He also conducts their journey and is its final destination.
rows.anchor: Arz’ı size zelûl kılan ve onun üzerinde yürümek salâhiyet[^22] ve kuvvetini veren O olduğu gibi, onda yürütecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should walk through divine grace with faith, fear, gratitude, obedience, just use of blessings, and striving in good works, avoiding disbelief, ingratitude, oppression, and sin.
rows.anchor: nimetlerinin kadrini bilip her birini yerinde sarf için ahsen-i amel ile mücahede ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can revoke humanity’s privilege to walk safely, make the earth quake beneath them, or subject them to someone stronger.
rows.anchor: Hâlık, dilediği zaman sizden o salâhiyeti alıverip size Arz’ı serkeşlendirerek altınızda çalkalayıvermeye

rows.speaker: بirtakım müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some exegetes take ‘the one in heaven’ to mean angels, since the title can include all rational beings above humanity.
rows.anchor: Onun için birtakım müfessirîn buna[^23] melâike demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context more clearly means the Creator, and this is also the predominant view transmitted from the early generations.
rows.anchor: Lâkin siyâk-ı kelâm bundan murad, Hâlık teâlâ’nın kendisi olmasında daha zâhirdir. Seleften menkul olan da ekseriyetle budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking God as physically contained in heaven raises the false implications that heaven exceeds Him in size or that He needs a created place, contrary to divine incomparability.
rows.anchor: semânın Allah’tan daha büyük olması veya O’nun da mahlûku olan ecsâm gibi mekâna muhtaç olması

rows.speaker: Müşebbihe
rows.claim: Anthropomorphists insist that God is physically in the sky; some also read fī as ʿalā to place Him over the Throne, as either located there or in a direction, which the author rejects as violating divine transcendence.
rows.anchor: Müşebbihe birçok vücûha muhtemil olmak itibariyle az çok müteşabih bulunan مَّن فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ’dan murad Allah demek olduğunda

rows.speaker: بعضları
rows.claim: Some harmonize the phrase with God’s Throne statement by reading fī as ʿalā, then differ over whether this means location or direction; the author says this conflicts with clear transcendence texts.
rows.anchor: burada عَلَى,فِى mânasına olarak semânın üzerinde yani fevkinde Arş üzerinde demek olduğunu söylemişler

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim İsfehânî
rows.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani suggests this addresses pagans who imagined God to be in heaven; the author rejects it because the broader address fits the discourse better.
rows.anchor: Ebû Müslim İsfehânî gibi bazıları da bu “Allah göktedir” diye zu‘meden müşriklerin zu‘mlarına göre bir hitab olduğuna zâhib olmak istemiş ise de

rows.speaker: بعضları
rows.claim: Some understand the phrase as God’s command operating in heaven, following verses that say He is God in heaven and earth and that He assigned each heaven its command.
rows.anchor: فِي ال َّسمَاءِ أَمْرهُ yani “hükmü, emri semâda cârî” demek olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: Selef
rows.claim: The early generations treated the phrase like the Throne verse as ambiguous, refrained from specifying its interpretation, and entrusted its intent to God while affirming that nothing resembles Him.
rows.anchor: Selef ise bunu da ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ [Tâ-hâ 20/5] gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author construes heaven as a symbol of absolute elevation above all created things, space, and time, so the phrase means God alone without bodily location or direction.
rows.anchor: Burada “semâ” gök dediğimiz cismânî semâdan ibaret değil, mutlak yükseklik, üstünlük remzidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Affirmations that God is in heaven, above heaven, or above the Throne aim to assert absolute transcendence and exclude indwelling; those who miss this meaning lapse into anthropomorphism.
rows.anchor: demekte ısrar edenlerin asıl maksadları da hulûlden tenzih ile bu ulüvv-i mutlakı isbattır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word samāʾ derives from elevation while Turkish gök is associated with color, so saying God is in samāʾ does not mean He is inside a solid physical sky.
rows.anchor: semâ ise mutlak yükseklik mânasına olan “sümüv”den müştak bulunduğu için “gök” tâbirinde tecsim, [5235] “semâ” tâbirinde yükseklik mânaları daha bâriz olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fī can express partial relation without containment or encompassing, as in saying the sky is over our heads and earth under our feet.
rows.anchor: فِى kelimesinin ifade ettiği zarfiyet-i cüz’iye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relation in ‘the one in heaven’ differs from that of a star in the sky; God’s elevation is like knowledge over sensation, Creator over creature, or ruler over subject.
rows.anchor: مَّن فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ kavlindeki zarfiyet ile اَلن َّجْمُ فِي ال َّسمَاءِ demekteki zarfiyet aynı mânada değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using fī rather than ʿalā conveys that divine elevation and lordship encompass inward and outward realms, not only what is above the heavens; this matches the verse on God in heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: O’nun ulviyeti zâhir ve bâtından, hâriç ve dâhilden muhît olduğunu, semânın yalnız üstünde değil, içinde dahi hükmünü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying God is in the earth is impermissible if it implies low location, but denying His divinity, worship, knowledge, or power there is false and can be unbelief; denial of spatial dwelling is sound.
rows.anchor: “Allah Arzdadır” demek câiz olamayacağında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God is in heaven and earth means He is worshipped there and knows secret and public things, not that His essence is spatially contained; He is greater than all creation.
rows.anchor: “semâvât ve Arz’da mâbud ilâhtır” diye anlamak lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s provision and walking lead toward God, while the reminder that provision is also in heaven calls people beyond earthly life; ascent brings the matching danger of decline, so the next verse warns them.
rows.anchor: bizi yalnız Arz’daki rızk ve hayat ile bırakmayıp وَفِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ رِزْقُكُمْ [ez-Zâriyât 51/22] ihtârı vechile semâda merzuk kılmak üzere kendisine davet buyurmakta olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first threat warns from within: God can make the docile earth swallow people or quake and boil beneath them, so they should fear Him and avoid rebellious injustice.
rows.anchor: Bu inzar Arz’ın zelûliyetini selb ile dâhilinden inzardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second threat warns from outside: although earth remains docile, God could send a messenger, angel, or wind from heaven to rain stones down like those hurled at devils.
rows.anchor: Arz’ın zelûliyeti durduğu hâlde hâricinden inzardır. Yani ya yoksa emin misiniz o semâdakinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You will know My warning’ can mean the sent warner or prophet, or the warning and threat conveyed through him; unbelievers will learn it in reality if they refuse faith now.
rows.anchor: Gönderdiğim nezîrim, peygamberim yahut onunla haber verdiğim inzârım, tehdîdim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from direct address to absent peoples as an example, swearing that earlier nations such as Noah’s, ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh’s, and Lot’s rejected their warners and were annihilated by dreadful punishment.
rows.anchor: Misâl için hitabdan gıyâba iltifattır. Yani nâm-ı celâlime kasem ile söylerim ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nezīr and nekīr correspond to nezīrī and nekīrī, with the first-person yā omitted; both can be verbal nouns or adjectives, and nekīr may mean an extraordinary punishment or its appointed force.
rows.anchor: “nezîr” “nezîrî”, “nekîr” “nekîrî” demektir. “Râ”nın kesresiyle mütekellim yâ’sından iktifâ olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse urges people to look at the birds above them, continuously spreading their wings like ranks and then folding them as they glide and descend.
rows.anchor: Bir düziye saflar düzer gibi mütemâdiyen kanat açıp süzülürken {وَيَقْبِضْنَ} ve yumarlarken?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds of every size, heavier than air, hover high and travel, find provision, attack prey, circle battlefields, take lives, and later flutter and fall; people should observe and learn.
rows.anchor: havadan ağır olan o sıkletleriyle bulutlar gibi yüksekte nasıl duruyor? Nasıl gidiyor, nasıl menzil alıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds have an inward impulse and will, yet in both activity and rest only the Merciful sustains them through the order and will that His mercy provides.
rows.anchor: kendi içlerinden gelen bir sevk, bir irade ile fâil olmakla beraber her iki hâlde de {مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ} onları ancak Rahmân tutuyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God’s command and permission, birds can descend from the heights at their appointed time and attack people on battlefields.
rows.anchor: müsaadesiyle sırası geldikçe tepelerinizden inip harb meydanlarında sizlere saldırıyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If birds violate the governing order, err, or lose their inner impulse, they immediately stop, tumble down, and perish.
rows.anchor: sevk kesiliverdiği vakit de derhâl tutulup yuvarlanıp düşüyor, helâk oluyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Merciful sees everything completely and watches over every state.
rows.anchor: gözetip duruyor. Bütün hayat, nüşûr hep O’na müntehî bulunuyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life and resurrection end with God; people walking on earth are like birds suspended in the air, held by the Merciful and able to rise only through His sustaining order.
rows.anchor: Sizi de tutan ve tutacak olan ancak O Rahmân’dır. Siz de O’nun onları uçuran nizâmı ve imsâki ile yükseklere uçabilirsiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should learn from birds and rise by relying on God’s will and following His order, building aircraft on earth and competing in the fields of trial.
rows.anchor: Arz’ın omuzları üstünde tayyareler yapın ve imtihan meydanlarında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: However high people fly, their aim should be reverence and worship, reaching resurrection, forgiveness, and reward, since no one escapes God’s forces or dominion.
rows.anchor: Fakat bütün hedefiniz ve gidişiniz O Rahmân’a karşı gelmek değil, O’na saygı ve ubûdiyet ile nezdinde nüşûra ermek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds, aircraft, and angels circling above are forces in the Merciful’s grasp; if people transgress, they can descend under His command to seize them.
rows.anchor: nice kuşlar, tayyareler, melekler vardır ki hepsi O Rahmân’ın kabza-i kudretinde cünûdudurlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the eye’s gaze eventually returns humbled and weary, people must turn back to their Creator and cannot escape His power.
